text:
Alex K: getting an alert — dedicated-eu-west2-gpu-pool-3 showing sustained latency spike starting ~2123456700, p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s, throughput down ~30% and tail retries increasing :warning:
InfraBot: automated alert: pool=d-eu-west2-3 metric=latency_p95 value=1.23s threshold=0.5s
Maya R: timeline? any config changes or rollouts in last hour?
Alex K: no deploys flagged. I see a big rise in eviction events + kernel-fallbacks in logs around the same time.
TJ: grabbing kernel selection logs now. Saw repeated lines like:
```
[2123456712] kernel_select: preferred=quantized_fast fallback=float_safe reason=mismatched_tensor_layout tenant=tc-82
[2123456713] kernel_select: fallback_path_taken count=87 pool=d-eu-west2-3
```
TJ: fallback frequency spiked which pushed more work onto slower kernels and increased per-token latency. :eyes:
Leah S: batcher traces show a shift in batch composition — many small, long-sequence requests got packed together. Effective batch token count hit max then caused KV cache thrash. Config snippet from the packer: ```max_batch_tokens=4096; sequence_split_threshold=1024; pack_policy=aggressive```
Priya N: KV cache miss rate jumped 9x at the same time (baseline ~2% -> ~18%), and KV churn correlated with eviction storms. Profiling summary (sample): p99_latency=1.41s, avg_kernel_time=0.98s, kv_miss_rate=18%
Alex K: putting it together: quota/placement allowed high-cardinality small tenants to co-locate on same GPUs. Aggressive pack_policy + long sequences caused oversized batches, triggering kernel fallback + KV cache eviction on hot shards -> noisy neighbor effect -> pool-level saturation.
Maya R: can we mitigate quickly? Options: 1) reduce packer aggressiveness 2) bump per-tenant placement isolation (soft pin) 3) throttle per-tenant concurrent tokens
Oncall Duty: applied quick mitigations at 2123457001 — set pack_policy=conservative on d-eu-west2-3 and limited tenant_concurrent_requests=4 for top noisy tenants. Monitoring now.
Alex K: after the change p95 dropped from 1.2s -> ~340ms within 90s, throughput recovering. Still seeing KV churn but much lower.
TJ: action items for next week: adjust kernel-selection to prefer quantized-safe fallback path earlier (avoid oscillation), add a fast-path for common sequence-length patterns, and add telemetry for fallback counts per-tenant.
Leah S: created follow-up ticket INF-4821 linking traces, profiler dumps, and tenant list (https://ok.redwood/INF-4821) — owner: Leah S, ETA: 72h.
Priya N: long-term: add per-tenant KV hot-shard guardrails (max entries, soft TTL) + sampling to identify tenants causing KV churn.
Maya R: also recommend a placement rule: prevent more than N small-tenants-per-GPU where "small" is <256 tokens avg over 5m. I'll draft change.
Oncall Duty: SLA notify sent to affected customers at 2123457150. No P1 escalations required now.
Alex K: thanks team. Will follow up in INF-4821 with root-cause writeup and the perf regression test to catch this in canaries. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: incident_state=mitigated severity=sev2 duration_seconds=565
Maya R: note: keep watch on kernel-fallback metric for 24h and roll back packer change only after stable.
TJ: I'll instrument fallback counters and add an alert for >5% fallback-rate per-pool.
Leah S: assigning postmortem to Alex K + Maya R + TJ. Target publish in 7d.
